A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adversarial Post-Training (APT) work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video user studies, COCO metrics, training ablations and inference-speed measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds original VBench video evaluation results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The architecture, consistency-distillation initialization, adversarial objectives, discriminator components and approximated R1 regularization are unchanged. Naming the pretrained model Seaweed in Section 3.1 identifies its provenance rather than establishing a model replacement.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation on VBench's 946 prompts alongside the retained custom video prompts and image benchmarks. This extends prompt coverage within the existing text-to-video task; no new modality or application domain is demonstrated.

E2.justification: New Table 7 evaluates consistency-distillation baselines at 1, 2 and 4 NFE alongside diffusion and APT. v1's reported video comparisons used the diffusion baseline. Image comparator membership is unchanged; newly cited SF-V and OSV are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added VBench protocol generates five videos per prompt and reports total, quality and semantic scores across specified inference-step budgets. Existing user-study procedures, COCO evaluation settings and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a limited analysis of whether increasing consistency-distillation inference steps closes the gap to APT, reporting results at 1, 2 and 4 NFE and persistent quality problems through 4 NFE. The existing component ablations and diagnostic analyses in Section 5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing seed and rater descriptions are retained, with no new repeated-evaluation statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. Five videos per VBench prompt specifies the new benchmark's sample size rather than an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports VBench total scores of 82.00/81.85 for APT at 1/2 steps, 67.05/74.20/77.97 for consistency at 1/2/4 steps, and 82.15 for diffusion at 25 steps, plus quality and semantic scores. These are additional benchmark outcomes; existing user-study, COCO, speed and illustrated results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–10 are unchanged. The VBench addition introduces no formal derivation, assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about one-step high-resolution video generation, competitive image generation and improved visual fidelity. The new benchmark supplies supporting evidence without changing these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B interprets VBench results as supporting APT's effectiveness and explicitly qualifies comparison with the 50-NFE diffusion model as unfair despite similar aggregate scores. Existing explanations and limitations concerning structural integrity, text alignment and video duration remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the previously unnamed pretrained model as Seaweed and explicitly describes the two-second videos as 49 frames. These are documentation refinements; the existing architecture specifications, optimizer, hardware, training budgets and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Five works are added: VBench, OSV, Seaweed, Phased Consistency Models and SF-V. Related work now distinguishes prior one-step image-to-video generation from APT's text-to-video setting. All earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Related-work paragraphs receive localized revisions, Appendix A becomes Image Quantitative Metrics, and the new video-metrics appendix shifts subsequent appendix labels. Figure 12's wording changes from non-cherry-picked to uncurated. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the VBench table, reorders the two COCO tables, and relocates the speed table as Table 8. Figure 12 receives caption edits and moves with its appendix. Existing image examples, diagrams and principal table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The VBench evaluation adds useful quantitative video evidence and explicit consistency-distillation comparisons that v1 lacked. Identifying the base model and acknowledging relevant image-to-video predecessors also improve transparency and positioning. These are limited gains: the existing evidence and acknowledged structural-integrity and text-alignment limitations remain unchanged.
